title: Isandro and the Confession
premise: Coral Voss, a meticulous true-crime podcaster, has spent seven years documenting the unsolved disappearance of a local girl — until a murdered man washes up wearing clothes stolen from Coral's own closet, making him both suspect and target. As he investigates, Coral discovers the town's most respected families closed the case years ago with a false confession bought from a vulnerable teenager, Isandro, who has just returned to town after his release. Racing a detective determined to pin the new murder on him, Coral must expose the real killer before Isandro is silenced again — and in doing so, finds the family he never had among the people brave enough to tell the truth.
about_author: L. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where they volunteer with a records-access nonprofit.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Coral Voss, POV. In his cluttered home studio, Coral records the 100th episode of his podcast on the seven-year-old disappearance of Marisol Quade, revealing how thoroughly he's cataloged the town's silences. The beat: lonely competence masking grief over his own estrangement from the community.

chapters.title: The Body in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Police wake him at dawn: a man found at the marina wears Coral's missing jacket and shirt, tags intact. Detective Rhea Solano treats him as suspect, not witness. Beat: shock curdling into the realization that someone wants the crime to wear his face.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Static
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Reviewing old interview tapes, Coral notices a voice he never identified on a background recording from the night Marisol vanished. Beat: obsessive hope rekindled; the cold case breathes again.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Confessed
chapters.summary: Isandro Reyes, POV. Recently released after serving time for a confession he made at sixteen, Isandro returns to town broke and watched. He recognizes Coral from the podcast. Beat: wary defiance; he knows what the confession cost and who profited.

chapters.title: Coffee and Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral tracks Isandro to a diner and interviews him off-record. Isandro recites the confession verbatim but its details don't match the evidence file. Beat: uneasy alliance formed between the man who built the case and the boy it was built on.

chapters.title: The Halloway Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Following money trails, Coral finds payments routed through the Halloway family's foundation to Isandro's former guardian. Beat: dread — the town's beloved first family funded the false confession.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Isandro visits the shoreline where Marisol was last seen and remembers what he actually saw that night: a car with a distinctive bumper sticker. Beat: guilt and terror entwined; memory returning is dangerous.

chapters.title: Solano's Warning
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Detective Solano confronts Coral: ballistics on the marina victim connect to an old case she was ordered to bury. She offers an uneasy truce. Beat: grudging respect; two investigators circling the same suppressed truth.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred One
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral airs an episode hinting the confession was coerced, withholding names. Downloads explode; so do threats. Beat: exhilaration followed by fear as anonymous messages quote details only the killer would know.

chapters.title: The House That Paid
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Isandro breaks into the shuttered Halloway boathouse and finds Marisol's backpack hidden in a wall cavity. Beat: vindication and horror — proof exists, and someone hid it well enough to kill for.

chapters.title: Family, However Found
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Coral shelters Isandro when his halfway house burns down suspiciously. Over takeout and case files, they become something like brothers. Beat: warmth — the found-family theme crystallizes amid danger.

chapters.title: The Widow's Version
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral interviews Evelyn Halloway, matriarch, whose polished grief slips once — she mentions a detail about Marisol never made public. Beat: quiet menace beneath civility; Coral leaves knowing she knows.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Someone torches Coral's studio; the archive survives only because Coral kept duplicates out of habit. A threatening note names Isandro as the next body. Beat: loss and resolve; the enemy is now hunting them openly.

chapters.title: Solano's Cold File
chapters.summary: Solano, POV. Solano secretly shares her buried file: the marina victim was the fixer who brokered the original confession. Beat: the conspiracy gains a shape — everyone who touched the lie is being erased.

chapters.title: The Bumper Sticker
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Isandro identifies the car from that night: a Halloway family vehicle, driven not by patriarch Richard but by his son Daniel, then nineteen. Beat: devastating clarity — the heir, not the patriarch, was behind the wheel.

chapters.title: Confession, Take Two
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral records Isandro recounting everything for the record, planning release if anything happens to them. Beat: solemnity; testimony becomes armor and target alike.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral infiltrates the Halloway charity gala and corners Daniel, playing back the discrepancy in his alibi. Daniel's composure cracks just enough. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Coral sees the killer see him seeing.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Isandro, POV. Isandro is abducted outside the diner by Daniel's fixer. He stalls, provokes, and memorizes every turn. Beat: terror sharpening into cunning; the boy who confessed falsely refuses to confess quietly again.

chapters.title: Where It Happened
chapters.summary: Coral and Solano, alternating POV. Decoding Isandro's dropped clues, Coral realizes Daniel is taking him to the original scene — the quarry — to finish the story properly. Beat: frantic urgency; history repeating unless interrupted.

chapters.title: The Quarry
chapters.summary: Coral, POV. Coral arrives as Daniel forces Isandro toward the water, recording everything on a live feed. Solano's team closes in; Daniel, exposed by his own need for a clean ending, is arrested as Isandro holds on. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at the site of the lie.

chapters.title: Marisol, Named
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The recording releases; Evelyn Halloway, protecting the family name no longer worth saving, confirms the cover-up. Marisol's remains are recovered and her mother finally hears the truth. Beat: catharsis; justice arrives outside the courtroom but inside the town's conscience.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: Coral and Isandro, dual POV. Months later, Coral ends the podcast series with Marisol's name spoken plainly, and Isandro — cleared, employed at Solano's precinct as a records clerk — moves into the room above Coral's rebuilt studio. Beat: belonging earned; the found family settles in for good.
